question: Version 8 kept the shape and randomised the settings. This keeps the settings and strips the shape: which structural commitment is each finding made of?
plain_language: A finding that survives having every one of its foundations removed was never a finding about anything. A finding that dies when you remove one specific thing tells you what it is made of -- and a claim with a named load-bearing commitment is a claim somebody can argue with.

commitments.generative: the reader models a maker producing the work, not a surface-to-label map
commitments.costly_attention: looking is expensive and the reader chooses
commitments.provenance_as_state: origin is inferred, and held apart from purpose
commitments.hierarchy: the maker has levels and the reader represents them
commitments.distributional: the reader holds a distribution, not a best guess
commitments.shared_likelihood: reader and maker draw on the same family: the body plan

sustained futile attention.note: this finding does not reproduce in the ablation harness's own baseline, so its row is UNINFORMATIVE rather than damning. The harness runs at reduced length and forced-attention budget to make a 4x7 grid affordable, and this finding is the one most sensitive to both. Its ablation row should not be read.

null_n41.statement: the label effect survives at least one ablation
null_n41.why: it has a 100% false-positive rate, so it cannot plausibly require all six commitments; if it does, the ablations are too destructive and this programme measures whether the model runs

null_n42.statement: at least one finding dies to at least one removal
null_n42.why: otherwise the ablations never reached the mechanism
